title: Detection of arboviruses in Aedes mosquito species in North Borneo
author: Ngiam, Ahmad, et al.

steps.title: Sort and pool mosquito specimens
steps.instruction: Identify Aedes mosquitoes using the taxonomic keys of Rattanarithikul (1982) and Jeffrey et al. (2023), discard non‑Aedes specimens, and place 1–5 mosquitoes per labelled 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube according to their capture coordinates.

steps.title: Homogenize samples and lyse cells
steps.instruction: For up to 25 pooled samples, add Buffer AL and carrier RNA, mix for ~2 min; homogenize manually and with the TGrinder H24 tissue grinder for 2–4 min total; incubate at 56 °C for 15 min; perform centrifugation, vortexing and a further room‑temperature incubation for ~6 min; add lysate and additional buffer and centrifuge for ~10 min; after the final spin the lysate is ready for RNA purification.

substeps.instruction: Mix mosquito pool with Buffer AL and carrier RNA (≈2 min).
Homogenize manually and automatically (2–4 min total).
Incubate at 56 °C for 15 min for cell lysis and RNA precipitation.
Centrifuge, vortex, then incubate at room temperature for ≈6 min.
Add lysate and buffer, centrifuge ≈10 min; sample is now ready for purification.

steps.title: Purify RNA with MinElute columns
steps.instruction: Apply the entire lysate onto a MinElute column avoiding the rim, centrifuge at 8000 rpm for 2 min, discard filtrate, then perform sequential washes with Buffer AW1, Buffer AW2, and ethanol, followed by a high‑speed dry spin and a brief heat‑dry step.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge column with lysate at 8000 rpm for 2 min; discard filtrate.
Place column in a clean 2 mL Wash Tube (WT).
Add 500 µL Buffer AW1, centrifuge at 11 000 rpm for 1 min; discard filtrate and replace WT.
Add 500 µL Buffer AW2, centrifuge at 11 000 rpm for 1 min; discard filtrate and replace WT.
Add ethanol (volume as per kit), centrifuge at 11 000 rpm for 1 min; discard filtrate and replace WT.
Centrifuge at 14 000 rpm for 3 min to dry the membrane completely.
Incubate the assembly at 56 °C for 3 min to ensure complete drying.

steps.title: Prepare real‑time PCR master mix
steps.instruction: Using the ZIKV/DENV/CHIKV Real‑Time PCR Kit (BioPerfectus, China), assemble a master mix that provides 20 µL per reaction; keep all components on ice and protected from light.

substeps.instruction: Combine kit reagents according to manufacturer instructions to obtain 20 µL master mix per reaction.
Maintain master mix on ice and shield from light.

steps.title: Set up PCR reactions and controls
steps.instruction: Dispense 20 µL master mix into each well or tube, add 5 µL purified RNA sample, include at least one positive control and one blank (negative) control per run, cap/seal, and briefly centrifuge to collect liquid at the bottom.

substeps.instruction: Place 20 µL master mix into each reaction vessel.
Add 5 µL RNA sample (or 5 µL control).
Ensure each run contains ≥1 positive control and ≥1 blank control.
Cap or seal vessels and centrifuge briefly to settle liquid.

steps.title: Run qPCR with specified cycling program
steps.instruction: Program the real‑time PCR instrument with the following thermal profile: 1 cycle reverse transcription at 50 °C for 10 min; 1 cycle initial denaturation at 95 °C for 5 min; 45 cycles of denaturation at 95 °C for 10 s followed by annealing/extension and fluorescence collection at 60 °C for 30 s (FAM for dengue, VIC for Zika, ROX for chikungunya).

substeps.instruction: Step 1 – Reverse transcription: 50 °C, 10 min (1 cycle).
Step 2 – Initial denaturation: 95 °C, 5 min (1 cycle).
Step 3 – Denaturation: 95 °C, 10 s (45 cycles).
Step 4 – Annealing/extension & signal collection: 60 °C, 30 s (45 cycles).

description: To validate the protocol, we demonstrated the outcome of using the protocol by using two regions of Sabah (Fig. 1), using a total of 352 female of Ae. aegypti (20), Ae. albopictus (273) and Ae. vexans (25), Ae. nivens (10), Ae. butleri (24) from Tawau; a total of 127 of mixture of Ae. aegypti (45), Ae. albopictus (56), Ae. vexans (15), Ae. butleri (11). The ZIKV/DENV/CHIKV Real-Time PCR Kit (BioPerfectus, China) was used. A master mix was prepared for each batch of samples, with 20 µL per reaction, followed by the addition of 5 µL of RNA sample. Samples were kept on ice and protected from light. Subsequently, 20 µL of master mix was placed into each reaction tube or plate, and 5 µL of isolated RNA or controls (positive or blank) was added. Each run included at least one positive control and one blank (negative) control. The reaction tubes or plate were capped or sealed, then centrifuged to ensure all liquid settled at the bottom. Finally, the real-time PCR instrument was set up with the appropriate conditions (Table 2).
